statement: The retained leaves contain several work streams and reused typescripts, rather than one continuous proof.

his_words: groupe de Raynaud; Un groupe diagonalisable est réflexif

statement: Under the initial flatness/reduced-fibre and connected geometric generic-fibre hypotheses on scan 48, a finite étale cover trivial on that fibre is asserted to descend to a finite étale cover of the normal integral base; the π₁ sequence follows.
reconstruction: The qualifier biréduit/réduit on scan 48 remains undecided. Properness is mentioned in comparison with a different fibre theorem, not securely imposed on this generic-fibre lemma.

his_words: Y loc. noeth. et univ. japonais; f_*(F) est constructible
statement: For a finite-type morphism to a locally noetherian universally Japanese base, the direct image of a constructible sheaf of finite sets is constructible.
reconstruction: Constructibility here is degree zero, not a statement about R¹ or finite generation.
check_reason: The exact hypotheses are visible. The incomplete SGA/§A/Standart reference is a reading alert, not an identification.

statement: For connected noetherian universally Japanese X, a finite locally closed partition X_i, and finite constant G, restriction H¹(X,G)→∏H¹(X_i,G) has finite fibres.
reconstruction: H¹ is the nonabelian torsor set; finiteness of each stratum set then gives finiteness on X.
check_reason: The universal-Japanese insertion is retained; the stronger finite-fibre formulation replaces a deleted assumption that the stratum sets were finite.

statement: The set of morphisms between constructible finite-set étale sheaves on a noetherian scheme is finite.
reconstruction: A common finite connected stratification and geometric stalks give an independent proof.
check_reason: The note matches the lemma and its proof mechanism; see independent_checks.md §1.

statement: For a noetherian universally Japanese S and finite G, global H¹-finiteness for every finite-type S-scheme is reduced to smooth affine maps with geometrically connected nonempty fibres over finite étale covers of normal integral affine subschemes of S, and to generic opens of those bases. A sufficient criterion uses geometric fibres and every subgroup H≤G×G on those bases; for abelian G it suffices to use G. Prime-to-residue-characteristic corollaries follow.
reconstruction: The detailed quantifiers are retained in the separate claim records; no replacement by just H¹(S,G) is allowed.
check_reason: The notes correctly identify the base-cover and subgroup quantifiers and distinguish equivalence from the sufficient condition.

his_words: H¹(X,G) est fini; topologiquement de génération finie
statement: Finiteness of H¹ for each finite target is weaker than topological finite generation of a profinite group.
reconstruction: The product ∏(Z/p_i)^{d_i} with distinct primes and unbounded d_i is an external counterexample to the inference, not a scheme constructed on the pages.
check_reason: The two types of statements occur in distinct arguments. The abstract counterexample was independently rechecked.

statement: In characteristic p, A¹ has infinitely many Z/p-torsors, so the prime-to-characteristic restriction cannot simply be removed from the affine H¹-finiteness statements.
reconstruction: Artin–Schreier classes x^m with p∤m supply the counterexample.
check_reason: The restriction is on the page; the Artin–Schreier computation is the earlier run’s explanatory example, now rechecked.

his_words: à fibres géom. connexes non vides, de dim 1
statement: The dimension induction requires an appropriate smooth dense-open fibration by geometrically connected curves, followed by treatment of the complement.
reconstruction: A generic projection and shrinking are a proposed completion, not an argument written in full on the page.
check_reason: The note identifies the missing geometric construction without replacing the curve-to-variety proposition’s quantifiers.

statement: For an algebraic scheme over an algebraically closed field of characteristic exponent p, the prime-to-p quotient is claimed finitely generated. A separate question asks finite generation after killing wild inertia at the codimension-one boundary of a proper normal compactification.
reconstruction: The boundary-tame quotient is not identified with the prime-to-p quotient. A later explicit formulation occurs on scan 64.
check_reason: The note preserves the difference between the announced prime-to-p theorem and the stronger tame question; Codex disagrees about finite generation versus finite presentation on scan 64.

statement: The local boundary condition means tame ramification, not absence of ramification; a prime-to-p Kummer extension is the basic example.
reconstruction: Modern terminology is supplied; the exact ramification-theoretic definition must be attached to the chosen valuation rings.
check_reason: Treating doux as étale would erase the inertia which the argument is studying.

statement: A finite étale cover of U×Y, geometrically tame along the codimension-one boundary after normalization and trivial on a selected fibre, is proposed to descend from a neighbourhood in Y. The passage from normal to nonnormal X is left to descent.
reconstruction: The dense-open, normalization, geometric generic-boundary, and rational-fibre qualifications are not interchangeable. Pro and Codex disagree on properness and theorem/question status.
check_reason: The warning is explicit. No completion of the nonnormal descent step is claimed by this review.

statement: The attempted Chow reduction does not ensure that the full inverse image of the omitted codimension-two set still has codimension at least two.
reconstruction: The blowup of a point on a smooth surface supplies a counterexample to this inference, not to the target finite-generation theorem.
check_reason: The transcribed clause is present and the codimension defect is real; whether it was an extra hypothesis must be decided on the scan.

statement: The proposal to replace irreducibility by connectedness in the generic-section argument is rejected on the page.
reconstruction: Two planes meeting in a point provide a modern explicit example.
check_reason: Both the question and the answer non are present; this is a local rejected strengthening, not a withdrawal of Bertini.

statement: The arbitrary-field statement needs geometric irreducibility to conclude irreducibility after the indicated algebraically closed generic parameter extension.
reconstruction: P²_C regarded over R refutes the ordinary-irreducibility reading. Later scan 113 explicitly supplies the geometric hypothesis (parent endpoint check).
check_reason: The note correctly flags the hypothesis gap; the later witness supplies a mathematical refinement, not an ink correction to scan 67.

statement: Under normality and geometric irreducibility over an algebraically closed base, a suitable generic complete-intersection section gives a surjection on π₁ by connectedness of pullbacks of finite étale covers.
reconstruction: The connected-cover criterion supplies the exact group-theoretic step; references and deformation to characteristic zero are separately indicated.
check_reason: The draft diagrams and the later corollary concern this same section argument; the note correctly keeps normality in the proof.

statement: For a fixed projective normal model and a codimension-two excluded set, a generic smooth projective curve of genus g avoiding that set gives the bound d(π₁(U))≤2g.
reconstruction: The asserted conclusion is a generator bound, not a presentation or a formula for π₁.
check_reason: The note matches the numerical bound and its dependence on a fixed curve.

statement: The notes reject a contextual claim that positive-characteristic fundamental groups of proper varieties are never known to be finitely presented. Modern results prove finite presentation for smooth projective varieties and subsequently all connected proper schemes over algebraically closed fields.
reconstruction: This is a correction to an earlier context packet, not a new manuscript theorem. Tame good-compactification hypotheses remain distinct from arbitrary boundary quotients.
check_reason: The alleged modern denial is not in the manuscript; the literature correction has exact modern sources and dates.

statement: A rational map from a regular open to a proper normal model is defined away from codimension two; purity handles its regular source, and normality of the target handles surjectivity on π₁.
reconstruction: The two roles are separated in the reconstruction. Pro dominant versus Codex normal remains a material reading disagreement.
check_reason: The note’s distinction is needed: normality alone does not justify purity of a singular source.

statement: Fixing one regular open in a projective normal model produces compatible surjections to the fundamental groups of all proper normal models; compactness then gives a surjection to their inverse limit and a finite generator bound.
reconstruction: Using a single source and the compactness argument is an explicit reconstruction of the compressed page.
check_reason: The reconstruction repairs the quantifier issue without assuming an unexplained uniform genus on every model.

statement: The system of π₁ of proper normal models is asked to be essentially constant; it is asserted to be so when a proper regular model exists.
reconstruction: A uniform generator bound alone is insufficient, as the cyclic inverse system Z/ℓ^m shows. General geometric stabilization is not settled by that abstract example.
check_reason: The conditional result and the unrestricted question are distinct on the page.

statement: For an arbitrary proper normal model X, does the regular locus U have the birational fundamental group, equivalently can each cover of U become étale on a proper modification?
reconstruction: The quotient (P¹×P¹)/±1 over C supplies a counterexample, with an a-adic valuation ramified in K(√a) preventing extension on every proper model.
check_reason: The valuation is part of the same counterexample and is merged, not counted as a second question; every hypothesis is checked in independent_checks.md §4.

statement: For a proper normal algebraic X and a codimension-two closed Y, is ker(π₁(X∖Y)→π₁(X)) topologically finitely generated?
reconstruction: The exact geometric question is retained; an abstract semidirect product only disproves deduction from finite generation of the surrounding groups.
check_reason: The note does not pretend to settle the geometric kernel question with an abstract example.

statement: The genus of a complete-intersection curve depends on the projective model and polarization; a uniform birational bound must use a chosen model once.
reconstruction: This is a clarification of the earlier commentary, not a separate authorial genus-invariance claim.
check_reason: No statement on the page declares that this genus is a birational invariant.

statement: The full étale product formula fails for A¹×A¹ in characteristic p, as shown by the Artin–Schreier torsor z^p−z=xy; the stated prime-to-p formula is not refuted.
reconstruction: The example is external to the manuscript and constrains a proposed strengthening.
check_reason: The note properly distinguishes the prime-to-p isomorphism from the full-product surjection.

statement: The dimension of the Picard scheme is at most its tangent dimension h¹(O), so a uniform h¹ bound implies a dimension bound; the converse and stabilization do not follow.
reconstruction: This is a general local-dimension inequality, separated from the author’s stronger hopes.

statement: Prime-to-p tame inertia is a quotient of the roots-of-unity module, with cyclotomic conjugation action of the base fundamental group.
reconstruction: A noncentral S₃ tame extension over F₂((t)) demonstrates why this is a module extension, not automatically a central extension.

reconstruction: It is not the complement of X₀ in the formal scheme, whose underlying topological space is X₀.

reconstruction: Extension to profinite I requires continuous cohomology and inverse-limit hypotheses; the finite-torsor proof alone does not give them.

statement: An unqualified vanishing of all higher cohomology on the tame universal cover of every smooth curve fails for P¹.

statement: For X₀=P¹ and normal degree d, the proposed π₂ quotient predicts prime-to-p cyclic inertia of order the prime-to-p part of |d| when d≠0, and infinite procyclic inertia when d=0.
reconstruction: This is an illustrative deduction conditional on the tame homotopy identification, not a separate computation performed on the page.
check_reason: The zero-degree case is essential and was checked explicitly.

statement: The extension class of the formal tame inertia sequence is to be identified with the restriction/pushforward of the Kummer Chern class of the normal bundle.

check_reason: The question and later proposed formula are the same task, and are merged.

statement: Vanishing of π₂ does not imply that the inertia extension splits: the class may remain nonzero in H² of π₁.

The later endpoint scan96, read for Stage5, explicitly asserts triviality; formal_elliptic_nonsplitting.md checks a finite tame algebraic covering and its completion.
check_reason: Within scans88–94 the note tests an implication; actual later scan96 makes the false splitting assertion explicit. Root owns that later claim and the cross-package merge.

statement: A fixed class with a fixed finite coefficient quotient vanishes at some finite tame cover if it vanishes in the filtered limit.
reconstruction: The finite stage depends on the coefficient quotient. One finite cover cannot generally kill all levels simultaneously.
check_reason: The exact finite quantifier is necessary for the intended construction.

statement: Divisibility of the normal-bundle class on U implies divisibility on X₀ modulo the classes of the boundary divisors, rather than ordinary divisibility in Pic(X₀).
reconstruction: For regular X₀ this follows from divisor localization and does not require the boundary divisors to be pairwise disjoint. Other proof steps may still do so.
check_reason: The deleted stronger inference and inserted boundary sum are both retained.

check_reason: The distinction repairs the relevant existence mechanism without endorsing the false unrestricted uniqueness statement.

reconstruction: Properness and a Mittag–Leffler condition in Lipman’s setting are a sufficient comparison, not a hypothesis present in this general formal setup.
check_reason: The inverse-limit issue is logically independent of the finite-level Kummer lifting argument.
